1 --- 2 title: io 3 description: API Reference for the io function. 4 --- 5 6 When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, Next.js needs you to decide whether to capture a synchronous value like `new Date()` or `Math.random()` once and reuse it for every visitor, or produce it fresh for each request. 7 8 To capture the value in the [static shell](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell), wrap it in [`"use cache"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache). To keep it out of the static shell, use `await io()`, which suspends during prerendering. 9 10 During a request, inside cached scopes, in the browser, and apps without Cache Components (including the Pages Router), calling `io()` resolves immediately. 11 12 ## Usage 13 14 Call `io()` to inform Next.js that an IO operation follows. 15 16 In a Server Component, call `await io()` before reading a value like `new Date()`, `Math.random()`, `crypto.randomUUID()`, or a synchronous database driver such as [`node:sqlite`](https://nodejs.org/api/sqlite.html): 17 18 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={13} switcher 19 import { Suspense } from 'react' 20 import { io } from 'next/cache' 21 22 export default function Page() { 23 return ( 24 Loading...

}> 25 26 27 ) 28 } 29 30 async function CurrentTime() { 31 await io() 32 return

{new Date().toISOString()}

33 } 34 ``` 35 36 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" highlight={13} switcher 37 import { Suspense } from 'react' 38 import { io } from 'next/cache' 39 40 export default function Page() { 41 return ( 42 Loading...

}> 43 44 45 ) 46 } 47 48 async function CurrentTime() { 49 await io() 50 return

{new Date().toISOString()}

51 } 52 ``` 53 54 In this route `CurrentTime` is wrapped in a `` boundary, during prerender, the `await io()` suspends and the fallback ships in the static shell. If `CurrentTime` were rendered inside a [`"use cache"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope instead, `io()` would be a no-op, the value is captured into the static shell and no `` boundary is required. 55 56 In a Client Component, call `io()` with React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) hook before reading a synchronous source like `Date.now()`. Client Components prerender on the server during SSR, where the read would otherwise be included in the static shell: 57 58 ```tsx filename="app/components.tsx" highlight={6} switcher 59 'use client' 60 import { use } from 'react' 61 import { io } from 'next/cache' 62 63 export function CurrentTime() { 64 use(io()) 65 return
{Date.now()}

{Date.now()}
77 } 78 ``` 79 80 ## When you don't need `io()` 81 82 - The component already uses a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) like `cookies()` or `headers()`. This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 712 713 For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 714 715 Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 716 717 If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 718 719 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 720 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 721 722 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 723 images: { 724 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 725 }, 726 } 727 728 export default nextConfig 729 ``` 730 731 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 732 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 733 const nextConfig = { 734 images: { 735 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 736 }, 737 } 738 739 module.exports = nextConfig 740 ``` 741 742 ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 743 744 The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 745 746 We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. Removing this setting reduces the size of the `srcset` attribute shipped to the browser by `next/image`. 747 748 If you need to support 16px images: 749 750 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 751 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 752 753 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 754 images: { 755 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 756 }, 757 } 758 759 export default nextConfig 760 ``` 761 762 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 763 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 764 const nextConfig = { 765 images: { 766 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 767 }, 768 } 769 770 module.exports = nextConfig 771 ``` 772 773 Rather than lack of developer usage, we believe 16 pixels width images have become less common, because `devicePixelRatio: 2` actually fetches a 32px image to prevent blurriness in retina displays. 774 775 ### `qualities` Default (Breaking change) 776 777 The default value for `images.qualities` has changed from allowing all qualities to only `[75]`. 778 779 If you need to support multiple quality levels: 780 781 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 782 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 783 784 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 785 images: { 786 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 787 }, 788 } 789 790 export default nextConfig 791 ``` 792 793 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 794 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 795 const nextConfig = { 796 images: { 797 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 798 }, 799 } 800 801 module.exports = nextConfig 802 ``` 803 804 If you specify a `quality` prop not included in the `image.qualities` array, the quality will be coerced to the closest value in `images.qualities`. For example, given the configuration above, a `quality` prop of 80, is coerced to 75. 805 806 ### Local IP Restriction (Breaking change) 807 808 A new security restriction blocks local IP optimization by default. Set `images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP` to `true` only for private networks. 809 810 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 811 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 812 813 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 814 images: { 815 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 816 }, 817 } 818 819 export default nextConfig 820 ``` 821 822 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 823 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 824 const nextConfig = { 825 images: { 826 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 827 }, 828 } 829 830 module.exports = nextConfig 831 ``` 832 833 This might be necessary when hosting Next.js in a VPC with split-horizon DNS and you receive status 400 Bad Request. Only enable once you understand the SSRF risk. 834 835 ### Maximum Redirects (Breaking change) 836 837 The default for `images.maximumRedirects` has changed from unlimited to 3 redirects maximum. 838 839 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 840 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 841 842 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 843 images: { 844 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 845 // or 846 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 847 }, 848 } 849 850 export default nextConfig 851 ``` 852 853 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 854 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 855 const nextConfig = { 856 images: { 857 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 858 // or 859 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 860 }, 861 } 862 863 module.exports = nextConfig 864 ``` 865 866 ### `next/legacy/image` Component (deprecated) 867 868 The `next/legacy/image` component is deprecated. Use `next/image` instead: 869 870 ```tsx 871 // Before 872 import Image from 'next/legacy/image' 873 874 // After 875 import Image from 'next/image' 876 ``` 877 878 ### `images.domains` Configuration (deprecated) 879 880 The `images.domains` config is deprecated. 881 882 ```js filename="next.config.js" 883 // image.domains is deprecated 884 module.exports = { 885 images: { 886 domains: ['example.com'], 887 }, 888 } 889 ``` 890 891 Use `images.remotePatterns` instead for improved security: 892 893 ```js filename="next.config.js" 894 // Use image.remotePatterns instead 895 module.exports = { 896 images: { 897 remotePatterns: [ 898 { 899 protocol: 'https', 900 hostname: 'example.com', 901 }, 902 ], 903 }, 904 } 905 ``` 906 907 ## Concurrent `dev` and `build` 908 909 `next dev` and `next build` now use separate output directories, enabling concurrent execution. The `next dev` command outputs to `.next/dev`. 910 911 Additionally, a lockfile mechanism prevents multiple `next dev` or `next build` instances on the same project. 912 913 The [Turbopack tracing command](/docs/app/guides/local-development#turbopack-tracing) should be: 914 915 ```bash package="pnpm" 916 pnpm next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 917 ``` 918 919 ```bash package="npm" 920 npx next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 921 ``` 922 923 ```bash package="yarn" 924 yarn next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 925 ``` 926 927 ```bash package="bun" 928 bunx next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 929 ``` 930 931 ## Parallel Routes `default.js` requirement 932 933 All [parallel route](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes) slots now require explicit `default.js` files. Builds will fail without them. 934 935 To maintain previous behavior, create a [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default) file that calls `notFound()` or returns `null`. 936 937 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 938 import { notFound } from 'next/navigation' 939 940 export default function Default() { 941 notFound() 942 } 943 ``` 944 945 Or return `null`: 946 947 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 948 export default function Default() { 949 return null 950 } 951 ``` 952 953 ## ESLint Flat Config 954 955 `@next/eslint-plugin-next` now defaults to ESLint Flat Config format, aligning with ESLint v10 which will drop legacy config support. 956 957 Make sure to review our API reference for the [`@next/eslint-plugin-next`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint#setup-eslint) plugin. 958 959 If you're using the legacy `.eslintrc` format, consider migrating to the flat config format. See the [ESLint migration guide](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide) for details. 960 961 ## Scroll Behavior Override 962 963 In **previous versions of Next.js**, if you had set `scroll-behavior: smooth` globally on your `` element via CSS, Next.js would override this during SPA route transitions, as follows: 964 965 1. Temporarily set `scroll-behavior` to `auto` 966 2. Perform the navigation (causing instant scroll to top) 967 3. Restore your original `scroll-behavior` value 968 969 This ensured that page navigation always felt snappy and instant, even when you had smooth scrolling enabled for in-page navigation. However, this manipulation could be expensive, especially at the start of every navigation. 970 971 In **Next.js 16**, this behavior has changed. By default, Next.js will **no longer override** your `scroll-behavior` setting during navigation. 972 973 **If you want Next.js to perform this override** (the previous default behavior), add the `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` attribute to your `` element: 974 975 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" 976 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 977 return ( 978 979 {children} 980 981 ) 982 } 983 ``` 984 985 ## Performance Improvements 986 987 Significant performance optimizations for `next dev` and `next start` commands, along with improved terminal output with clearer formatting, better error messages, and improved performance metrics. 988 989 **Next.js 16** removes the `size` and `First Load JS` metrics from the `next build` output. We found these to be inaccurate in server-driven architectures using React Server Components. Both our Turbopack and Webpack implementations had issues, and disagreed on how to account for Client Components payload. 990 991 The most effective way to measure actual route performance is through tools such as [Chrome Lighthouse](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview) or Vercel Analytics, which focus on Core Web Vitals and downloaded resource sizes. 992 993 ### `next dev` config load 994 995 In previous versions the Next config file was loaded twice during development: 996 997 - When running the `next dev` command 998 - When the `next dev` command started the Next.js server 999 1000 This was inefficient because the `next dev` command doesn't need the config file to start the Next.js server. 1001 1002 A consequence of this change is that, when running `next dev` checking if `process.argv` includes `'dev'`, in your Next.js config file, will return `false`. 1003 1004 > **Good to know**: The `typegen`, and `build` commands, are still visible in `process.argv`. 1005 1006 This is specially important for plugins that trigger side-effects on `next dev`. If that's the case, it might be enough to check if `NODE_ENV` is set to `development`. 1007 1008 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1009 import { startServer } from 'docs-lib/dev-server' 1010 1011 const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' 1012 1013 if (isDev) { 1014 startServer() 1015 } 1016 1017 const nextConfig = { 1018 /* Your config options */ 1019 } 1020 1021 module.exports = nextConfig 1022 ``` 1023 1024 Alternatively, use the [`phase`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js#phase) in which the configuration is loaded. 1025 1026 ## Build Adapters API (alpha) 1027 1028 Following the [Build Adapters RFC](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77740), the first alpha version of the Build Adapters API is now available. 1029 1030 Build Adapters allow you to create custom adapters that hook into the build process, enabling deployment platforms and custom build integrations to modify Next.js configuration or process build output. 1031 1032 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1033 const nextConfig = { 1034 experimental: { 1035 adapterPath: require.resolve('./my-adapter.js'), 1036 }, 1037 } 1038 1039 module.exports = nextConfig 1040 ``` 1041 1042 `adapterPath` was promoted to a stable, top-level option in 16.2.0. See [`adapterPath`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/adapterPath) for the current API reference. 1043 1044 ## Modern Sass API 1045 1046 `sass-loader` has been bumped to v16, which supports [modern Sass syntax](https://sass-lang.com/documentation/js-api/#md:usage) and new features. 1047 1048 ## Removals 1049 1050 These features were previously deprecated and are now removed: 1051 1052 ### AMP Support 1053 1054 AMP adoption has declined significantly, and maintaining this feature adds complexity to the framework. All AMP APIs and configurations have been removed: 1055 1056 - `amp` configuration from your Next config file 1057 - `next/amp` hook imports and usage (`useAmp`) 1058 1059 ```tsx 1060 // Removed 1061 import { useAmp } from 'next/amp' 1062 1063 // Removed 1064 export const config = { amp: true } 1065 ``` 1066 1067 - `export const config = { amp: true }` from pages 1068 1069 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1070 const nextConfig = { 1071 // Removed 1072 amp: { 1073 canonicalBase: 'https://example.com', 1074 }, 1075 } 1076 1077 module.exports = nextConfig 1078 ``` 1079 1080 Evaluate if AMP is still necessary for your use case. Most performance benefits can now be achieved through Next.js's built-in optimizations and modern web standards. 1081 1082 ### `next lint` Command 1083 1084 The `next lint` command has been removed. Use Biome or ESLint directly. `next build` no longer runs linting. 1085 1086 A codemod is available to automate migration: 1087 1088 ```bash package="pnpm" 1089 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1090 ``` 1091 1092 ```bash package="npm" 1093 npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1094 ``` 1095 1096 ```bash package="yarn" 1097 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1098 ``` 1099 1100 ```bash package="bun" 1101 bunx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1102 ``` 1103 1104 The `eslint` option in the Next.js config file is also removed. 1105 1106 ```js filename="next.config.mjs" 1107 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 1108 const nextConfig = { 1109 // No longer supported 1110 // eslint: {}, 1111 } 1112 1113 export default nextConfig 1114 ``` 1115 1116 ### Runtime Configuration 1117 1118 `serverRuntimeConfig` and `publicRuntimeConfig` have been removed. Use environment variables instead. 1119 1120 **Before (Next.js 15):** 1121 1122 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1123 module.exports = { 1124 serverRuntimeConfig: { 1125 dbUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL, 1126 }, 1127 publicRuntimeConfig: { 1128 apiUrl: '/api', 1129 }, 1130 } 1131 ``` 1132 1133 ```tsx filename="pages/index.tsx" 1134 import getConfig from 'next/config' 1135 1136 export default function Page() { 1137 const { publicRuntimeConfig } = getConfig() 1138 return

API URL: {publicRuntimeConfig.apiUrl}

1139 } 1140 ``` 1141 1142 **After (Next.js 16):** 1143 1144 For server-only values, access environment variables directly in Server Components: 1145 1146 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1147 async function fetchData() { 1148 const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL 1149 // Use for server-side operations only 1150 return await db.query(dbUrl, 'SELECT * FROM users') 1151 } 1152 1153 export default async function Page() { 1154 const data = await fetchData() 1155 return
{/* render data */}
1156 } 1157 ``` 1158 1159 > **Good to know**: Use the [taint API](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/taint) to prevent accidentally passing sensitive server values to Client Components. 1160 1161 For client-accessible values, use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix: 1162 1163 ```bash filename=".env.local" 1164 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="/api" 1165 ``` 1166 1167 ```tsx filename="app/components/client-component.tsx" 1168 'use client' 1169 1170 export default function ClientComponent() { 1171 const apiUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL 1172 return

API URL: {apiUrl}

1173 } 1174 ``` 1175 1176 To ensure environment variables are read at runtime (not bundled at build time), use the [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function before reading from `process.env`: 1177 1178 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1179 import { connection } from 'next/server' 1180 1181 export default async function Page() { 1182 await connection() 1183 const config = process.env.RUNTIME_CONFIG 1184 return

{config}

1185 } 1186 ``` 1187 1188 Learn more about [environment variables](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables). 1189 1190 ### `devIndicators` Options 1191 1192 The following options have been removed from [`devIndicators`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/devIndicators): 1193 1194 - `appIsrStatus` 1195 - `buildActivity` 1196 - `buildActivityPosition` 1197 1198 The indicator itself remains available. 1199 1200 ### `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` 1201 1202 The `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` flags have been removed. 1203 1204 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1205 // Before: experimental.useCache 1206 module.exports = { 1207 experimental: { 1208 useCache: true, 1209 }, 1210 } 1211 ``` 1212 1213 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1214 // Before: experimental.dynamicIO 1215 module.exports = { 1216 experimental: { 1217 dynamicIO: true, 1218 }, 1219 } 1220 ``` 1221 1222 If you were actively using these flags, migrate to top-level [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents): 1223 1224 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 1225 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 1226 1227 // After 1228 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 1229 cacheComponents: true, 1230 } 1231 1232 export default nextConfig 1233 ``` 1234 1235 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 1236 // After 1237 module.exports = { 1238 cacheComponents: true, 1239 } 1240 ``` 1241 1242 If you were not actively adopting Cache Components, remove the flags instead. Enabling `cacheComponents` is not a rename-only change: it can surface build errors for uncached data outside of `` and requires adopting the Cache Components model. 1243 1244 For the full migration path, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components). 1245 1246 ### `unstable_rootParams` 1247 1248 The `unstable_rootParams` function has been removed. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean. 58 59 60 ``` 61 62 ## Using the codemod 63 64 To update to Next.js version 16, you can use the `upgrade` [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160): 65 66 ```bash package="pnpm" 67 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 68 ``` 69 70 ```bash package="npm" 71 npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 72 ``` 73 74 ```bash package="yarn" 75 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 76 ``` 77 78 ```bash package="bun" 79 bunx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 80 ``` 81 82 The [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to: 83 84 - Update `next.config.js` to use the new `turbopack` configuration 85 - Migrate from `next lint` to the ESLint CLI 86 - Migrate from deprecated `middleware` convention to `proxy` 87 - Remove `unstable_` prefix from stabilized APIs 88 - Remove `experimental_ppr` Route Segment Config from pages and layouts 89 90 The `upgrade` codemod does not run every migration codemod. If your app still uses synchronous `params`, `searchParams`, `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `draftMode()` access from the Next.js 15 compatibility period, also run the async Request APIs codemod: 91 92 ```bash filename="Terminal" 93 npx @next/codemod@canary next-async-request-api . 94 ``` 95 96 ## Install packages manually 97 98 If you prefer to do it manually, install the latest Next.js and React versions: 99 100 ```bash package="pnpm" 101 pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 102 ``` 103 104 ```bash package="npm" 105 npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 106 ``` 107 108 ```bash package="yarn" 109 yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 110 ``` 111 112 ```bash package="bun" 113 bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 114 ``` 115 116 If you are using TypeScript, ensure you also upgrade `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` to their latest versions. 117 118 ## Node.js runtime and browser support 119 120 | Requirement | Change / Details | 121 | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | 122 | Node.js 20.9+ | Minimum version now `20.9.0` (LTS); Node.js 18 no longer supported | 123 | TypeScript 5+ | Minimum version now `5.1.0` | 124 | Browsers | Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+ | 125 126 ## Turbopack by default 127 128 Starting with **Next.js 16**, Turbopack is stable and used by default with `next dev` and `next build` 129 130 Previously you had to enable Turbopack using `--turbopack`, or `--turbo`. 131 132 ```json filename="package.json" 133 { 134 "scripts": { 135 "dev": "next dev --turbopack", 136 "build": "next build --turbopack", 137 "start": "next start" 138 } 139 } 140 ``` 141 142 This is no longer necessary. You can update your `package.json` scripts: 143 144 ```json filename="package.json" 145 { 146 "scripts": { 147 "dev": "next dev", 148 "build": "next build", 149 "start": "next start" 150 } 151 } 152 ``` 153 154 If your project has a [custom `webpack`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/webpack) configuration and you run `next build` (which now uses Turbopack by default), the build will **fail** to prevent misconfiguration issues. 155 156 You have a few different ways to address this: 157 158 - **Use Turbopack anyway:** Run with `next build --turbopack` to build using Turbopack and ignore your `webpack` config. 159 - **Switch to Turbopack fully:** Migrate your `webpack` config to Turbopack-compatible options. 160 - **Keep using Webpack:** Use the `--webpack` flag to opt out of Turbopack and build with Webpack. 161 162 > **Good to know**: If you see failing builds because a `webpack` configuration was found, but you don't define one yourself, it is likely that a plugin is adding a `webpack` option 163 164 ### Opting out of Turbopack 165 166 If you need to continue using Webpack, you can opt out with the `--webpack` flag. For example, to use Turbopack in development but Webpack for production builds: 167 168 ```json filename="package.json" 169 { 170 "scripts": { 171 "dev": "next dev", 172 "build": "next build --webpack", 173 "start": "next start" 174 } 175 } 176 ``` 177 178 We recommend using Turbopack for development and production. Submit a comment to this [thread](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77721), if you are unable to switch to Turbopack. 179 180 ### Turbopack configuration location 181 182 The `experimental.turbopack` configuration is out of experimental. 183 184 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 185 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 186 187 // Next.js 15 - experimental.turbopack 188 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 189 experimental: { 190 turbopack: { 191 // options 192 }, 193 }, 194 } 195 196 export default nextConfig 197 ``` 198 199 You can use it as a top-level `turbopack` option: 200 201 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 202 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 203 204 // Next.js 16 - turbopack at the top level of nextConfig 205 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 206 turbopack: { 207 // options 208 }, 209 } 210 211 export default nextConfig 212 ``` 213 214 Make sure to review the `Turbopack` configuration [options](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack). **Next.js 16** introduces various improvements and new options, for example: 215 216 - [Advanced Webpack loader conditions](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#advanced-webpack-loader-conditions) 217 - [debugIds](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#debug-ids) 218 219 ### Resolve alias fallback 220 221 In some projects, client-side code may import files containing Node.js native modules. This will cause `Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs'` type of errors. 222 223 When this happens, you should refactor your code so that your client-side bundles do not reference these Node.js native modules. 224 225 However, in some cases, this might not be possible. In Webpack the `resolve.fallback` option was typically used to **silence** the error. Turbopack offers a similar option, using `turbopack.resolveAlias`. In this case, tell Turbopack to load an empty module when `fs` is requested for the browser. 226 227 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 228 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 229 230 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 231 turbopack: { 232 resolveAlias: { 233 fs: { 234 browser: './empty.ts', // We recommend to fix code imports before using this method 235 }, 236 }, 237 }, 238 } 239 240 export default nextConfig 241 ``` 242 243 It is preferable to refactor your modules so that client code doesn't ever import from modules using Node.js native modules. 244 245 ### Sass node_modules imports 246 247 Turbopack fully supports importing Sass files from `node_modules`. Note that while Webpack allowed the legacy tilde (`~`) prefix, Turbopack does not support this syntax. 248 249 In Webpack: 250 251 ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 252 @import '~bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 253 ``` 254 255 In Turbopack: 256 257 ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 258 @import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 259 ``` 260 261 If changing the imports is not possible, you can use `turbopack.resolveAlias`. For example: 262 263 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 264 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 265 266 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 267 turbopack: { 268 resolveAlias: { 269 '~*': '*', 270 }, 271 }, 272 } 273 274 export default nextConfig 275 ``` 276 277 ### Turbopack File System Caching 278 279 Turbopack stores compiler artifacts on disk between runs, for significantly faster compile times across restarts. Filesystem caching is enabled by default for both `next dev` and `next build`, through `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev` and `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild`. See [Turbopack FileSystem Caching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopackFileSystemCache) to configure or disable either one. 280 281 ## Async Request APIs (Breaking change) 282 283 Version 15 introduced [Async Request APIs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-15#async-request-apis-breaking-change) as a breaking change, with **temporary** synchronous compatibility. 284 285 Starting with **Next.js 16**, synchronous access is fully removed. These APIs can only be accessed asynchronously. 286 287 - [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) 288 - [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) 289 - [`draftMode`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/draft-mode) 290 - Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 716 717 If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 718 719 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 720 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 721 722 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 723 images: { 724 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 725 }, 726 } 727 728 export default nextConfig 729 ``` 730 731 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 732 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 733 const nextConfig = { 734 images: { 735 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 736 }, 737 } 738 739 module.exports = nextConfig 740 ``` 741 742 ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 743 744 The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 745 746 We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. 2	title: route.js
3	description: API reference for the route.js special file.
4	---
5	
6	Route Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.
7	
8	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
9	export async function GET() {
10	  return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })
11	}
12	```
13	
14	```js filename="route.js" switcher
15	export async function GET() {
16	  return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })
17	}
18	```
19	
20	## Reference
21	
22	### HTTP Methods
23	
24	A **route** file allows you to create custom request handlers for a given route. The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`.
25	
26	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
27	export async function GET(request: Request) {}
28	
29	export async function HEAD(request: Request) {}
30	
31	export async function POST(request: Request) {}
32	
33	export async function PUT(request: Request) {}
34	
35	export async function DELETE(request: Request) {}
36	
37	export async function PATCH(request: Request) {}
38	
39	// If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.
40	export async function OPTIONS(request: Request) {}
41	```
42	
43	```js filename="route.js" switcher
44	export async function GET(request) {}
45	
46	export async function HEAD(request) {}
47	
48	export async function POST(request) {}
49	
50	export async function PUT(request) {}
51	
52	export async function DELETE(request) {}
53	
54	export async function PATCH(request) {}
55	
56	// If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.
57	export async function OPTIONS(request) {}
58	```
59	
60	### Parameters
61	
62	#### `request` (optional)
63	
64	The `request` object is a [NextRequest](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) object, which is an extension of the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) API. `NextRequest` gives you further control over the incoming request, including easily accessing `cookies` and an extended, parsed, URL object `nextUrl`.
65	
66	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
67	import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
68	
69	export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
70	  const url = request.nextUrl
71	}
72	```
73	
74	```js filename="route.js" switcher
75	export async function GET(request) {
76	  const url = request.nextUrl
77	}
78	```
79	
80	#### `context` (optional)
81	
82	- **`params`**: a promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) for the current route.
83	
84	```ts filename="app/dashboard/[team]/route.ts" switcher
85	export async function GET(
86	  request: Request,
87	  { params }: { params: Promise<{ team: string }> }
88	) {
89	  const { team } = await params
90	}
91	```
92	
93	```js filename="app/dashboard/[team]/route.js" switcher
94	export async function GET(request, { params }) {
95	  const { team } = await params
96	}
97	```
98	
99	| Example                          | URL            | `params`                           |
100	| -------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
101	| `app/dashboard/[team]/route.js`  | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>`           |
102	| `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/route.js` | `/shop/1/2`    | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` |
103	| `app/blog/[...slug]/route.js`    | `/blog/1/2`    | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>`    |
104	
105	### Route Context Helper
106	
107	You can type the Route Handler context using `RouteContext` to get strongly typed `params` from a route literal. `RouteContext` is a globally available helper.
108	
109	```ts filename="app/users/[id]/route.ts"
110	import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
111	
112	export async function GET(_req: NextRequest, ctx: RouteContext<'/users/[id]'>) {
113	  const { id } = await ctx.params
114	  return Response.json({ id })
115	}
116	```
117	
118	> **Good to know**
119	>
120	> - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build` or `next typegen`.
121	> - After type generation, the `RouteContext` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported.
122	
123	## Examples
124	
125	### Cookies
126	
127	You can read or set cookies with [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) from `next/headers`.
128	
129	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
130	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
131	
132	export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
133	  const cookieStore = await cookies()
134	
135	  const a = cookieStore.get('a')
136	  const b = cookieStore.set('b', '1')
137	  const c = cookieStore.delete('c')
138	}
139	```
140	
141	```js filename="route.js" switcher
142	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
143	
144	export async function GET(request) {
145	  const cookieStore = await cookies()
146	
147	  const a = cookieStore.get('a')
148	  const b = cookieStore.set('b', '1')
149	  const c = cookieStore.delete('c')
150	}
151	```
152	
153	Alternatively, you can return a new `Response` using the [`Set-Cookie`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie) header.
154	
155	```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher
156	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
157	
158	export async function GET(request: Request) {
159	  const cookieStore = await cookies()
160	  const token = cookieStore.get('token')
161

--- title: not-found.js description: API reference for the not-found.js file. --- Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases: - **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment. - **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page. ## `not-found.js` The **not-found** file is used to render UI when the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment. Along with serving a custom UI, Next.js will return a `200` HTTP status code for streamed responses, and `404` for non-streamed responses (see [Status Codes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes) for details about SEO). ```tsx filename="app/not-found.tsx" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function NotFound() { return (

Not Found

Could not find requested resource

Return Home
) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/blog/not-found.js" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function NotFound() { return (

Not Found

Could not find requested resource

Return Home
) } ``` In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `not-found.js` renders between `loading.js` and `page.js`. It is wrapped by the `` boundary from `loading.js` and the error boundary from `error.js` in the same segment. > **Good to know**: The default not found UI follows the operating system's color scheme via `prefers-color-scheme` and does not read an app-level theme (such as a class or `data-theme` attribute on ``). Because it renders inside your root layout, the quickest way to match an explicit theme is to add a higher-specificity rule pair in your global stylesheet, scoped to your theme selector — for example `html[data-theme='light'] body` and `html[data-theme='dark'] body`. For full control over the markup, provide your own `not-found.js`. ## `global-not-found.js` (experimental) The `global-not-found.js` file lets you define a 404 page for your entire application. Unlike `not-found.js`, which works at the route level, this is used when a requested URL doesn't match any route at all. Next.js **skips rendering** and directly returns this global page. events.content:
Migration complete and verified. The `pages` directory is gone, everything now runs on the App Router, and both the production build and a live smoke test pass (SSR user-agent renders, per-post titles resolve, 404 works, API handlers return 200/201/400/405 correctly).

Because this project runs a Next.js 16.4 canary, I followed the bundled docs in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` rather than the historical APIs — two things there differ from older App Router versions: error boundaries receive a **`retry()`** prop (not `reset()`), and `params`/`headers()` are **async-only** (the Next 15 sync fallback is removed).

What each old file became:

- **`_app.js` + `_document.js` → `app/layout.tsx`** — root layout with `<html>`/`<body>`, the header/nav/footer shell, `AppProvider`, and a `metadata` export for the description and favicon. The Google Fonts `<link>` tags became `next/font/google`'s `Inter` (weights 400/500/600, `display: swap`), which handles preconnect automatically.
- **`index.js` (`getServerSideProps`) → `app/page.tsx`** — async Server Component; `req.headers['user-agent']` became `await headers()` from `next/headers`, and the fetch uses `cache: 'no-store'` (the `getServerSideProps` equivalent). Confirmed dynamic (`ƒ`) in the build output.
- **`blog/index.js` (`getStaticProps` + `revalidate: 60`) → `app/blog/page.tsx`** — fetch with `next: { revalidate: 60 }` (ISR, shows `1m` revalidate in the build).
- **`blog/[id].js` (`getStaticPaths`/`getStaticProps`) → `app/blog/[id]/page.tsx`** — `generateStaticParams` prerenders the first 10 posts; `fallback: 'blocking'` maps to `dynamicParams = true`; `notFound: true` became `notFound()`; the `next/head` tags became `generateMetadata` with awaited `params: Promise<{ id: string }>`; `router.isFallback` is obsolete and was dropped.
- **`404.js` → `app/not-found.tsx`**, **`_error.js` → `app/error.tsx` + `app/global-error.tsx`** — both error boundaries are Client Components using this version's `retry()` prop; `Error.getInitialProps` has no App Router equivalent and the status-code branching is now handled by the not-found/error split.
- **`pages/api/*` → `app/api/posts/route.ts` and `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts`** — the `handler(req, res)` if/else chains became per-method `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE` exports returning `NextResponse.json()`; `req.query.id` became the awaited `params` promise; unsupported methods get an automatic 405 (verified with PATCH).
- **`next/router` usages** — the `router.push`/`router.back` buttons moved into small typed Client Components (`components/NavigateButton.tsx`, `components/BackButton.tsx`) using `useRouter` from `next/navigation`; `AppProvider` was converted to a typed `.tsx` Client Component with a `'use client'` directive it previously lacked.

Everything is TypeScript with explicit types (`Metadata`, promise-typed `params`, a shared `Post`/`Comment` model in `lib/types.ts`). One note: `next build` auto-added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `tsconfig.json`'s include — that's expected behavior in Next 16.
